blindSummary:
This state is an unusual case for trans visitors: risk of enforcement is very low, because it is small and popular among tourists (museums, a great religious site and its adjoining square) with essentially no resident jurisdiction a traveller can fall afoul of. Nothing about being trans is criminalised; there are no bathroom inspections, no morality police, and neither the ceremonial foreign-guard unit nor the state's small police force polices tourists' gender expression. Millions of tourists of every presentation visit annually without incident; entry is open, with no border formality.

The doctrinal climate is hostile: a 2024 declaration by the state's religious authority condemned gender-affirming surgery and so-called "gender theory" as violations of human dignity, and there is obviously no legal recognition or protection of any kind. But this is a climate signal, not a traveller-facing mechanism — the realistic worst case for a visitor is being refused entry to the great religious site over a dress-code dispute (shoulders/knees rules apply to everyone).
blindOutOfScope: Doctrinal positions are climate signals; state employment and religious-law matters are resident-facing.

Wire service: the head of state - the reigning religious leader - endorsed same-sex civil unions in a 2020 documentary about him, a landmark statement that gay couples deserve legal protection in civil-union laws (page largely navigation content at fetch time).

LGBTQ+ news outlet (Oct 2008): the state blocked the appointment of an openly gay foreign career diplomat - himself party to a registered civil union with a same-sex partner - as envoy, also rejecting a divorced candidate; the church was quoted as being 'opposed to gay rights and any attempts to protect or recognise gay relationships in law'.

Religion-news wire (June 2021): in a historic first, the state invoked its sovereign status under the treaty with the single surrounding state that established its modern sovereignty to protest that state's draft anti-homophobia law, via a formal diplomatic note from its state secretariat, objecting that it could restrict the state religion's freedom to teach.

Educational document of the state religious authority (2019), on 'gender theory' in education: it opposes the concept as 'denying the difference and reciprocity in nature of a man and a woman' and 'eliminating the anthropological basis of the family'.
